notes: City of Kimball, fiscal year ended Sept 30, 2025. Governmental funds are modified cash basis; enterprise funds (Electric, Water, Sewer, Trash, Landfill) are accrual. Basis recorded as 'cash' (governmental roll-forward uses fund balances = cash, CDs and county treasurer cash, no liabilities): beginning_cash = Sept 30 2024 total fund balances 1,733,110 (p7, marked computed); ending_cash = total assets of Total Governmental Funds 1,429,032 (p5). Governmental receipts/disbursements from Total Governmental Funds column (p7). Identity: 1,733,110 + 3,090,168 - 3,364,921 + 277,871 - 307,196 = 1,429,032. Business-type: Statement of Revenues, Expenses and Changes in Fund Net Position, Total enterprise column (pp10-11); receipts = sales, occupation taxes, other revenue, interest income, grant income; disbursements = operating expenses (5,362,022) + interest expense 295,409 + bond fees 60,875 (= total business-type expenses 5,718,306 on p2). Loss on disposal of equipment (336) is in business_type.other_financing as -336. Check: 10,853,106 + 6,672,650 - 5,718,306 + 366,384 - 336 = 12,173,498. Printed totals are not given as single lines for business-type, so receipts 6,672,650 is summed (operating revenues 6,203,857 + nonoperating 468,793). The governmental internal service fund (593,770 revenue, 584,266 expense, net position 190,129) is a governmental-activities fund not in the governmental funds statement and is excluded. Component unit (Airport Authority) excluded. Proprietary cash flow statement (pp12-13) not recorded because basis is cash (proprietary null). Balance sheet = government-wide Statement of Net Position, Total primary government column (p1); governmental funds balance sheet on pp4-5 not used. Detail: General Fund departments schedule (pp19-20) is more detailed than the General Fund budget schedule (p14), so only the departments schedule is entered (budget p14 actuals identical to totals; budget figures not entered). Department columns were each entered per object line; the Total column was not entered. Department functions tie to the statement: Administrative = General government 236,264; Police + Fire = Public safety 933,051 + capital outlay/debt (91,751 split into capital outlay 71,603, principal 18,475, interest 1,673); Park + Pool + Library = Environment and leisure 484,582; Cemetery = Public works 187,954. Salaries and benefits entered as salaries and wages (benefits not separated). Street, Golf and Economic Development budget schedules entered (actuals); blank/dash actuals omitted. Nonmajor combining statement entered per fund (Fire Equipment, Keno, Fines; Handyman and Community Development funds had no activity). Bond Fund has no schedule. Utility fund budget schedules are not in the trimmed PDF. Transfer cross-check: governmental transfers in 277,871 (General 180,671 + Golf 97,200) and out 307,196 (General); net -29,325 differs from the -366,384 interfund transfers on the Statement of Activities because the latter includes the internal service fund (-337,059) and business-type transfer 366,384 (enterprise funds net +366,384); GF transfers out 307,196 are on the statement as transfers (not included in spending); the unmatched amount (net 29,325 out of governmental funds vs 366,384 into enterprise funds incl. the internal service fund 337,059) is explained by that internal service fund, so the difference reconciles: 29,325 + 337,059 = 366,384. Read pages 1-20 of 20.

decision_needed.question: Governmental transfers out (307,196) exceed transfers in (277,871) by 29,325, while enterprise funds report 366,384 of net transfers in. Is the 337,059 internal service fund transfer the whole difference?
decision_needed.recorded_as: governmental transfers in 277,871 / out 307,196; business_type.transfers_net +366,384, as printed
